properties.chose: Anthony, 2026-10-01: "we'll have to make the '--call' option work as best we can", after his organisation declined to allow reflow2 as an MCP server (dec:idea-where-an-org-blocks-third-party-mcp-ask-for-an-allowlist-before-building-around-it). The door goes from a build-script convenience to a supported way for an agent to work a design. That widens rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground, and a dated note there says so. The pieces (a served instructions file from init, skill stubs, a harness name, a CI probe) and the door improvements in the sibling ideas are ordered in the plan, once Anthony confirms the order.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's ideas 1, 7, 8 and 11 in using_call.md (branch feat/vscode-call-door, 2026-10-01), from fact:field-report-vscode-copilot-with-mcp-blocked-reaches-reflow2-only-through-the-call-door-2026-10-01.

THE IDEAS, in his words:
(1) "A served CLI-door instructions file from `reflow2 init`": a harness such as `--harness vscode-cli` writes `.github/instructions/reflow2.instructions.md`, served from the binary so `reflow2 update` keeps it current. Fixes limitation 11 and "makes the setup committable for a team".
(7) "Skill stubs VS Code can discover": `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` holding only frontmatter plus one line, "run `reflow2 --call get_skill …` and follow it". The body stays served (thin install preserved).
(8) "A harness name for the door": `REFLOW2_HARNESS=vscode` or `--harness` under `--call`, so usage_report attributes calls.
(11) "A CI probe for the door, the way a harness is tested": tools/test_call_door.py drives the binary the way the instructions tell an agent to.

WHAT IS CHEAP: (8) is a flag on the client name. (11) mostly re-drives cases the existing --call test already has, plus a held-graph write and an export. (1) reuses the served-pointer mechanism (req:thin-install).

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside it: rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground makes "can call an MCP server" reflow2's ONE assumption about an agent. Non-MCP mechanisms ship only as ADDITIONS, never as what a capability rests on. A supported door for agents with no MCP widens who reflow2 is for, which is Anthony's call and not a packaging detail. It also has a cost: every served instruction and skill would have to stay true in two dialects ("call X" and "--call X").
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-01 — the `--call` door becomes a supported route for an agent that cannot use MCP; which pieces land, and in what order, is planned separately
